newsitem.title: USA: US late spot gasoline reclaims lost ground.
newsitem.headline: US late spot gasoline reclaims lost ground.

text.p: U.S. spot gasoline jumped about two cents a gallon by late Friday, reclaiming ground lost Thursday as the NYMEX pendulum swung back into positive territory, players said.
Differentials were little changed on New York Harbor gasoline grades, but apparent tightness in the Gulf Coast helped firm conventional unleaded M3-grade about 0.30 cents, players said.
The strength on gasoline was apparently a function of shrinking gasoline runs at the nations refineries and slimmer imports, traders said.
Distillate buyers were hard to find at both centers. Heating oil diffs in the Gulf and New York Harbor have held fairly steady, meanwhile, amid volatile NYMEX movements during the week.
"That indicates there's not a lot of serious pressure on physical supplies yet," one trader said.
Prompt two oil in New York stayed near even with November NYMEX on Friday, while Gulf Coast prompt material was stable with offers at about 2.60 cents below the print.
